requirements.title: COMMAND_ARGUMENT_COUNT result is a default integer scalar
requirements.definition: The result characteristics of COMMAND_ARGUMENT_COUNT are default integer scalar.

pending.command_argument_count-default-integer-s: Compile and run a program with a default integer variable initialized to -99, assign COMMAND_ARGUMENT_COUNT() to it with no command arguments, and assert the value is exactly 0; the scalar/default-integer use is load-bearing because assigning to an array or noninteger context would not exercise this result characteristic.

requirements.title: COMMAND_ARGUMENT_COUNT reports the number of available command arguments, with zero for none
requirements.definition: The result value is the number of command arguments available; with no command arguments, or no processor support for command arguments, the value is zero; a command name, if the processor has one, is not counted as an argument.

pending.command_argument_count-no-arguments-zero: Run the fixture with no user command arguments, initialize the result variable to -99 before the call, and assert COMMAND_ARGUMENT_COUNT() returns exactly 0. This remains valid whether the processor supports command arguments or not.
pending.command_argument_count-counts-available-: No portable conformance oracle requires nonzero for a run supplied with extra host command arguments, because the same sentence permits processors without command-argument support to return zero. Do not bind a nonzero-count fixture without a separately established processor-support profile.
pending.command_argument_count-command-name-not-: The no-user-argument fixture also proves any processor command name is not counted, because the only conforming result in that execution is 0.

requirements.title: COMMAND_ARGUMENT_COUNT command-argument support and command-name concept are processor latitude
requirements.definition: The processor may lack command-argument support, and only processors that have a command-name concept apply the command-name exclusion.

pending.command_argument_count-support-may-be-ab: No portable oracle may require support for host command arguments or a nonzero result when extra host arguments are supplied; the exact portable fixture is the no-argument zero case.
pending.command_argument_count-command-name-conc: No portable oracle may require that the processor expose or define a command-name concept; tests assert only that zero user arguments produce zero.
